setupSteps: Warm up first. Do 2 to 5 minutes of walking or marching on the spot, or stretch after a workout, so the muscles are warm. Do not stretch cold muscles hard.
Floor. Flat, non-slip floor. Bare feet or a sticky mat; shoes with a flat sole are fine for the calf stretch. No socks on tiles.
Wall. Stand an arm's length from a smooth, clear wall. A chair or countertop works for the quad stretch.
Clothing. Shorts, leggings or loose pants rolled up so the knee can bend fully. A long kurta can be tucked at the waist.
Towel or strap. Keep a hand towel or belt ready if you cannot reach your foot without rounding your back.
Camera. Phone on a shelf at hip height, 2 to 2.5 m to the side, so hip, knee, ankle and heel are in frame (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Stand tall beside the wall
steps.action: stand with the left hand flat on the wall at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
steps.visualCheck: side view, ear over shoulder over hip over ankle.

steps.title: Shift weight onto the wall-side leg
steps.action: press the left foot into the floor and keep the left knee soft but nearly straight.
steps.visualCheck: hips level; standing knee not locked back.

steps.title: Bend the free knee
steps.action: bend the right knee and lift the heel toward your buttock.
steps.feel: the foot floats up behind you; no pinch behind the knee.
steps.visualCheck: side view, the right thigh stays pointing straight down.

steps.title: Hold the foot
steps.action: reach back with the right hand and hold the ankle (or loop a towel around it). Keep the knees close together.
steps.feel: mild pull along the front of the thigh.
steps.breathing: slow nose breaths; do not hold the breath.
steps.visualCheck: do not hold the toes or twist the ankle sideways.

steps.title: Tuck the pelvis slightly
steps.action: gently tuck the tailbone under, as if zipping the lower belly in. Do not pull the knee forward or behind.
steps.feel: the stretch moves higher into the front of the thigh and hip; the low back stays long.
steps.visualCheck: side view, no arch in the low back, ribs down.

steps.title: Hold
steps.tempo: 30 seconds (chosen; sources give 15 to 30 seconds, 30 to 45 seconds and 30 seconds).
steps.visualCheck: head tall, standing knee soft, thigh pointing down.

steps.title: Release and switch
steps.action: let the foot down slowly, shake the leg, repeat on the other side. Do 2 rounds per side.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Face the wall
steps.action: stand an arm's length away, hands flat on the wall at chest height.
steps.visualCheck: side view, body in a straight line when leaning.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Step the left foot back
steps.action: step the left foot back about one big stride (about 60 to 90 cm, est.). Point both feet straight at the wall.
steps.visualCheck: feet parallel, toes not turned out.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Bend the front knee
steps.action: bend the right knee. Keep the back leg straight and the back heel flat on the floor.
steps.feel: a pull in the upper calf of the back leg.
steps.visualCheck: side view, back knee straight, heel down.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Lean in
steps.action: lean the hips toward the wall, bending the arms, until you feel a gentle pull.
steps.feel: mild stretch in the big calf muscle.
steps.visualCheck: head, spine and back leg in one line from the side.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Hold
steps.action: stay still; keep the arch of the back foot gently lifted and the foot facing forward.
steps.feel: mild tension, no sharp pain at the heel or Achilles.

steps.part: B. Wall calf stretch, straight back knee (gastrocnemius)
steps.title: Release and switch. Step in, shake out, repeat on the other leg. 2 rounds per side

steps.part: C. Wall calf stretch, bent back knee (soleus)
steps.title: Start as in B (step 1 and 2)

steps.part: C. Wall calf stretch, bent back knee (soleus)
steps.title: Bend the back knee
steps.action: keep the back heel down and bend the back knee, moving it forward toward the wall (over the toes), while the front knee also bends slightly.
steps.feel: the stretch moves lower in the calf, nearer the Achilles.
steps.visualCheck: side view, back heel stays on the floor, knee moves forward in line with the second toe.

steps.part: C. Wall calf stretch, bent back knee (soleus)
steps.title: Sink gently
steps.action: lower the hips a little; stop before any sharp pain.
steps.feel: mild pull lower in the calf.

steps.part: C. Wall calf stretch, bent back knee (soleus)
steps.title: Hold. 30 seconds, slow breathing

steps.part: C. Wall calf stretch, bent back knee (soleus)
steps.title: Release and switch. 2 rounds per side

commonMistakes.title: Bouncing
commonMistakes.text: Bouncing. Bouncing or jerking can trigger the muscle to tighten and risks a strain. Fix: ease in, hold still.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the low back in the quad stretch
commonMistakes.text: Arching the low back in the quad stretch. The stretch then goes to the back, not the thigh. Fix: tuck the tailbone slightly and keep the knees close together.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling the heel too hard to the buttock
commonMistakes.text: Pulling the heel too hard to the buttock. It can strain the knee. Fix: stop at mild tension; use a towel or a half-way position.

commonMistakes.title: Back heel lifting in the calf stretch
commonMistakes.text: Back heel lifting in the calf stretch. The calf is not stretched. Fix: step the foot back less far and press the heel down.

commonMistakes.title: Back foot turned out
commonMistakes.text: Back foot turned out. It shifts the stretch and twists the ankle and knee. Fix: point both feet straight to the wall.

commonMistakes.title: Bent back knee when you wanted the big calf muscle
commonMistakes.text: Bent back knee when you wanted the big calf muscle. Straight-knee stretches the gastrocnemius; bent-knee goes to the soleus. Fix: use the version that matches the muscle you want, and do both.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath or going to pain
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath or going to pain. Tension rises and the muscle resists. Fix: breathe slowly; stretch to mild tension.

commonMistakes.title: Stretching cold or right before power work
commonMistakes.text: Stretching cold or right before power work. Long static holds just before sprinting, jumping or lifting heavy can slightly reduce performance (Behm 2016; see section 7). Fix: warm up with dynamic movement first, and keep static holds short before hard efforts.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the heel off a step with an Achilles problem
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the heel off a step with an Achilles problem. Stepped heel drops are advised against by NHS-affiliated leaflets for insertional Achilles tendinopathy unless a physio says so. Fix: use the flat floor wall stretch only, and ask a professional.

safetyNotes: Mild tension, never pain. Sources agree: stop at pain in the knee, ankle or Achilles.
Knee: the standing quad stretch compresses the knee most; with knee pain use the side-lying or half-kneeling version, a padded mat, and a shorter hold. Do not force the heel to the buttock.

Ankle and Achilles: a gentle floor-level wall stretch is common advice, but NHS-affiliated leaflets say not to do stepped heel drops with insertional Achilles tendinopathy, and some say calf stretches for Achilles problems should follow advice from a physio or podiatrist. A sudden pain, swelling or a pop in the back of the lower leg needs medical attention.
Warm muscles only: warm up first; do not do hard static stretches cold or immediately before sprinting or heavy lifts.
Balance: use the wall for the standing quad stretch; skip it if you cannot balance on one leg safely.

Stop immediately if you feel: sharp or burning pain, joint pain, pins and needles, numbness, sudden dizziness, a pop, or calf pain with swelling, redness or warmth (see a doctor urgently, possible clot).
Spotter: not needed; use a wall or chair.
Gym etiquette: use the stretching area or a clear wall space, not the walkways or racks.

Hold time: sources range from 10 to 60 seconds with 2 to 5 repetitions. We chose 30 seconds, 2 rounds per side.

Static before exercise: long static holds just before power work may slightly reduce performance, but within a full warm-up the effect is unclear. We chose dynamic movement before exercise and static holds after.
Standing quad stretch for sore knees: sources suggest side-lying or half-kneeling. We offer both and use the wall for the standing version.
Clinical evidence that calf stretching is useful: only small gains in ankle dorsiflexion (a few degrees) and unclear clinical importance. Stated honestly.
Quad-and-calf-specific MET, joint-angle norms, and hold-time dose-response: Not found. Our thresholds are estimates.
Pose-specific condition sources (most rows; ACOG pregnancy wording; clinical knee OA guidance; osteoporosis stretching): Not found.
Official AYUSH or MDNIY text: Not found for this item (it is not a named asana).
Most pages were seen only as search snippets; direct page fetches were not possible.
